13	 * `ProductListSearchHit`/`RawImage` pattern, mirrored below for `CartLineItem`/`CartItemImage`).
14	 *
15	 * Disclosed design choice, not a directly sourced requirement (flagged per this step's own
16	 * instructions): `ProductItem`/`ItemVariantProvider` (`overrides/app/components/product-item/
17	 * index.tsx:140`, `overrides/app/components/item-variant/index.tsx:43`) both currently declare
18	 * their real data-carrying prop as the raw untyped basket/product object itself
19	 * (`product`/`variant`, both `SfccProduct`/`SfccVariant = any`) — today's leaves read every
20	 * display field (image, name, combined attributes) directly off that object via
21	 * `useItemVariant()`, not from individually-mapped props. This mapper is, per this step's plan
22	 * text, "an as-yet-unused-by-anything-else container-layer function" — it does not change or
23	 * feed either of those two files (out of this step's scope). What it produces instead is a pure,
24	 * tested equivalent of the specific per-field computations those leaves and
25	 * `product-quantity-picker.tsx`/`use-derived-product.js` already perform internally off that same
26	 * raw object (image+alt, combined colour/size, quantity, stepQuantity) — ready for whichever
27	 * future step decides how a real page hands data down, without having modified any of those
28	 * existing files.
29	 *
30	 * `CartLineItem` models the REAL runtime shape a basket line item has by the time it reaches
31	 * those leaves: the un-overridden base cart page never passes the raw `basket.productItems[i]`
32	 * alone — it merges it with the matching full `Product` (fetched separately via `useProducts`)
33	 * before handing it down: `product={{...productItem, ...productsByItemId[productItem.itemId],
34	 * price: productItem.price, quantity: ...}}` (see
35	 * `node_modules/@salesforce/retail-react-app/app/components/product-item-list/index.jsx`, the
36	 * `<ProductItem product={...}>` call). `imageGroups`/`variationAttributes`/`variationValues`/
37	 * `stepQuantity`/`name` all come from that merged-in `Product` half, not from
38	 * `ShopperBasketsTypes.ProductItem` itself (confirmed against its generated fields — it has no
39	 * image/variation/stepQuantity fields at all beyond its own `{[key: string]: any}` catch-all).
40	 *
41	 * Both halves are `Pick`'d, not intersected raw (zm-tester, SFCC-11 step 3.4 finding): the real
42	 * generated `ProductItem` type carries the identical `{[key: string]: any}` catch-all the comment
43	 * above already calls out on `Product`. Intersecting it raw would silently resolve a typo'd field
44	 * name (or a nonexistent one) to `any` instead of a compile error — empirically confirmed harmless
45	 * today (every real access below is spelled correctly) but a real, latent gap a future edit could
46	 * hit silently. `Pick`ing both halves closes it the same way on both sides.
47	 */
48	type CartLineItem = Pick<ShopperBasketsTypes.ProductItem, 'itemId' | 'productId' | 'quantity' | 'productName'> &
49	  Pick<
50	    ShopperProductsTypes.Product,
51	    'imageGroups' | 'variationAttributes' | 'variationValues' | 'stepQuantity' | 'name'
52	  >;
53	
54	type CartItemImage = {
55	  src?: string;
56	  /**
57	   * Always a string, never undefined — even when there's no image at all (falls back to the
58	   * item's own name, then `''`). See `selectCartItemImage`'s own doc comment for the fallback
59	   * chain and why this differs from `productListCardMapper.ts`'s `toCardImage`, which returns
60	   * `undefined` for the whole image on a miss instead.
61	   */
62	  alt: string;
63	};
64	
65	type CartItemMapperResult = {
66	  itemId?: string;
67	  productId?: string;
68	  name: string;
69	  image: CartItemImage;
70	  combinedAttributes: string;
71	  quantity?: number;
72	  stepQuantity: number;
73	};
74	
75	/**
76	 * Matches `node_modules/@salesforce/retail-react-app/app/hooks/use-derived-product.js:38`'s own
77	 * `product?.stepQuantity || 1` exactly — reused as a value, not a shared import, since that hook
78	 * itself isn't a pure function this module can call (it's stateful, `useState`-backed).
79	 */
80	const DEFAULT_STEP_QUANTITY = 1;
81	
82	/**
83	 * Selects this line item's display image, always returning a defined `alt` even when there is no
84	 * image at all (unlike `productListCardMapper.ts`'s `toCardImage`, which returns `undefined` for
85	 * the whole image on a miss — a PLP card can legitimately skip rendering entirely when it has
86	 * nothing to show; a cart line item cannot, per this step's own pass criteria).
87	 *
88	 * The lookup itself reuses `findImageGroupBy` exactly as
89	 * `overrides/app/components/item-variant/item-image.tsx:70-73` already does (same `viewType:
90	 * 'small'` / `selectedVariationAttributes` call) rather than reimplementing image-group matching.
91	 */
92	const selectCartItemImage = (item: CartLineItem): CartItemImage => {
93	  const image = findImageGroupBy(item.imageGroups, {
94	    viewType: 'small',
95	    selectedVariationAttributes: item.variationValues,
96	  })?.images?.[0];
97	
98	  return {
99	    src: image?.disBaseLink || image?.link,
100	    alt: image?.alt || item.productName || item.name || '',
101	  };
102	};
103	
104	/**
105	 * Combines the colour and size variation values into the single string the Figma cart-item spec
106	 * calls for, reusing the exact mechanism
107	 * `overrides/app/components/item-variant/item-attributes.tsx:98,148-150` already uses for its own
108	 * `combineAttributeValues` behaviour (`getDisplayVariationValues(...)` then
109	 * `Object.values(...).join(', ')`) rather than reimplementing string-combining from scratch.
110	 *
111	 * Ordering is inherited from that same call, not independently re-sorted here: it reflects
112	 * whichever order the incoming `variationValues` object's own keys are in (see
113	 * `getDisplayVariationValues`'s `Object.entries(values).reduce(...)`,
114	 * `node_modules/@salesforce/retail-react-app/app/utils/product-utils.js:30`). This is the
115	 * identical mechanism `item-attributes.tsx`'s own docblock (line 31) already cites as producing
116	 * "Lilac Sand, One size" (colour, size) for real Zimmermann catalog data —
117	 * `product-item/index.tsx`'s docblock (line 44) corroborates the same combined-string behaviour
118	 * generically ("colour, size") without repeating that specific example. This function inherits
119	 * that already-verified behaviour rather than re-guaranteeing the order independently.
120	 */
121	const selectCombinedAttributes = (item: CartLineItem): string => {
122	  const variationValues = getDisplayVariationValues(item.variationAttributes, item.variationValues);
123	  return variationValues ? Object.values(variationValues).join(', ') : '';
124	};
125	
126	/**
127	 * Maps one basket line item (already merged with its full product data — see this file's own
128	 * module docblock) to a plain display-data shape: image, name, one combined colour/size string,
129	 * and quantity/stepQuantity passed through. Pure function, no hooks — keeps every consumer in B3
130	 * prop-driven with no data-fetching hook in a leaf, per this step's own plan text.
131	 */
132	export const selectCartItemProps = (item: CartLineItem): CartItemMapperResult => ({
133	  itemId: item.itemId,
134	  productId: item.productId,
135	  name: item.productName || item.name || '',
136	  image: selectCartItemImage(item),
137	  combinedAttributes: selectCombinedAttributes(item),
138	  quantity: item.quantity,
139	  stepQuantity: item.stepQuantity || DEFAULT_STEP_QUANTITY,
140	});

# SFCC-11 Cart bundle — BUILD HANDOFF
**Written 2026-09-17, end of the planning session. Read this first, then the two files below.**

Everything needed to build is already written down. **Do not re-derive it.** If something here
disagrees with your own reading of the cards or the design, this file and its two companions win —
they were produced with the live sources open and every claim checked.

## Read in this order

| File | Lines | What it is |
|---|---|---|
| **this file** | — | state, entry point, what NOT to redo |
| `zimmermann-pwa/.claude/session-notes.md` §1–§11.11 | 971 | every AC adjudicated, every decision with its rationale and rejected alternatives, the complete Figma spec (51 nodes, 4 breakpoints, atom-level), every divergence |
| `.runs/SFCC-11/plan.md` | 909 | file manifest with tiers/owners, the 18 commits, per-step pass criteria, loop config |
| `.runs/SFCC-11/findings.md` | 184 | the gate — 18 findings, re-run twice, **no 🔴** |

**Order of authority inside `plan.md`:** §11 supersedes §2 (scale). §9 supersedes B1's original
scope. §10 closes the three content questions. §8 records corrections to the planner's own output.
§3 (manifest) and §4 (steps) are unchanged and authoritative.

## Repo state at handoff

```
current branch   feature/SFCC-831-689_country-language-mismatch   (clean, carries open PR #112)
develop          71025f18  == origin/develop                     (fast-forwarded this session)
tsc --noEmit     exit 0, clean baseline
```

**First action:**
```bash
git checkout develop && git pull --ff-only && git checkout -b feature/SFCC-11_cart
```
Never branch from the current branch — it carries PR #112.

## The shape

**One branch, one PR, 18 commits.** Commit order and messages: `plan.md` §11.
Step boundaries ARE commit boundaries. One commit per step, never more.

**The one hard gate: commit 4.** Copy-first — eight files copied, converted, `tsc` clean, markers
added, then **STOP**. Nothing proceeds until Marcel has observed all eight markers firing from
**three surfaces**: the cart, the account wishlist page, and a checkout summary. A machine cannot
score this step.

**The one adversarial pass: commit 13.** Prove `useIsMutating()` by making it fail on purpose first.

**Commit 18 last, deliberately** — the trigger. Nothing is shopper-reachable until then. It carries
a **regression check**, not a light pass: `product-view` is consumed by the PDP, the quick-view
modal and the bonus-product modal.

## Settled — do not reopen

- The drawer **replaces both** the OOTB `AddToCartModal` and the `/cart` page. Base files stay
  mounted, just uncalled. `/cart` goes vestigial.
- The trigger is **SFCC-315's own scope** ("triggered from any surface on the site").
- ~~`maxOrderQuantity = product?.c_maxOrderQuantity ?? MAX_PURCHASE_QUANTITY`~~ — **superseded by
  plan.md's own step 3.4 text (§4), found stale by zm-tester during commit 10 and corrected here
  per this same document's own authority rule two paragraphs below ("§3/§4 are unchanged and
  authoritative"): the bare `??` above lets `0`/negative through uncaught, which step 3.4's actual
  pass criteria explicitly forbid. What was built instead: `getMaxOrderQuantity()`
  (`overrides/app/utils/maxOrderQuantity.ts`) validates for a finite, positive number and falls
  back to its own independent constant (3) — deliberately NOT shared with `MAX_PURCHASE_QUANTITY`,
  since the TSD's real resolution order means a shared constant would need reworking the day the
  real per-site BM preference ships. Still true, unaffected by this correction: the cart already
  receives the full unfiltered product payload.
- Override **both** `product-item` (3 files) and `item-variant` (5 files). 8 files total.
- Per-line enforcement, `>=` not `==`, `sum_quantities`, consolidate to one line at 3.

  (`overrides/app/hooks/use-toast.ts` **does not exist** — that was a bad path from a
  forward-looking `protectedFiles.md` entry).
- `PlusIcon` ported to `zimm.tsx`; Pay marks exported from Figma and committed to
  `overrides/app/assets/svg/`.
- Stepper: 24px invisible touch target via `ZimmButton`'s `icon` size, 8px gap.
- Stacked messages drop the product name; the interim toast uses the product-named copy.
- 25px raw values → snap to 24, with a comment.
- No UI-designer message. Divergences are annotated inline per `zimmButton.css.ts`'s pattern.
- **Out of scope for now (Marcel, 2026-09-17):**
  `feature/SFCC-836-317_cart-ui-zimmermann-benefits-icon-text-contentful` — a branch pushed today
  building the Zimmermann Benefits component that composes inside our drawer. Not our concern this
  build. Recorded so nobody re-raises it mid-flight.

PASS. Ship it. Nothing in this step should slow the branch down.

## Why that's the right call

This is 4 files, ~200 lines of pure TypeScript, zero rendered output, and I could not break it. I re-ran every cheap gate myself and then went further — I edited the real files twice (typo, then deleted a validation check), watched them fail exactly the way they should, and put them back byte-identical (MD5-verified, `git status` clean after). Both attacks are detailed below.

| Axis | Verdict | Evidence |
|---|---|---|
| **Correctness** | PASS | `tsc --noEmit`: 0 errors. `npm run test`: 95 files, 1322 tests green, including the exact expected new counts (`cartItemMapper.test.ts` 5, `maxOrderQuantity.test.ts` 6). Lint: 963/896/67, unchanged from baseline, zero hits on either new file (grepped full output myself). |
| **Pass criteria** | PASS | All 4 criteria in plan.md:324-328 met with evidence, not assertion — detail below. |
| **Conformance** | PASS | `type` not `interface`, `unknown`+guard not `any`, `Pick` not raw intersection, named constants not magic numbers, correct base-path imports for reused SFCC utils, zero `console`/`debugger`/live `any`/non-null-assertion in either file (grepped directly). |
| **Restraint** | PASS | Orchestrator verdict IN SCOPE; I independently matched all 4 files against plan.md's own manifest and found nothing extra, nothing missing. No Tier 1/2 file touched — `git status` shows only the 3 new paths. `product-detail/index.tsx` (the Hard Rule #5 tripwire) has zero diff. |
| **Completeness** | PASS | Both source files have a co-located `.test.ts`. No story owed — neither file renders anything, and the named precedent (`productListCardMapper.ts`) also ships test-only. |
| **Design fidelity** | **N/A**, not UNVERIFIED | I read both files end-to-end: no JSX, no component, no theme/recipe touch, no rendered output at all. The "visual checkpoint owed" rule only applies when a step changes what renders — this one structurally cannot. There's no Figma node to hold it against. |

## What I tried to falsify

1. **The headline technical claim — that `Pick`ing both halves of `CartLineItem` instead of intersecting the raw SDK types actually catches something.** I backed up `cartItemMapper.ts`, typo'd `item.productName` to `item.produtcName`, ran `tsc`. Got exactly `TS2551: Property 'produtcName' does not exist on type 'CartLineItem'. Did you mean 'productName'?` — restored the file, MD5 matched pre-edit, `tsc` clean again. This is the third independent reproduction of this claim (Tester, Orchestrator, now me) and it holds every time.
2. **The mutation-tested "Infinity" gap in `maxOrderQuantity.ts`.** Backed up the file, deleted `Number.isFinite(value)` from the guard, ran just that test file. Result: exactly 1 failure (the Infinity test, `expected Infinity to be 3`), the other 5 tests still green. That test is load-bearing, not decorative. Restored, MD5 matched, full suite re-green.
3. **Pass criterion 3's grep, taken literally rather than on faith.** Ran `grep -rn "useCurrentBasket\|useProduct\|commerce-sdk-react" overrides/app/components/ui-kits/**/zimmCart* overrides/app/components/product-item overrides/app/components/item-variant` myself — it does **not** come back empty, it hits real code in `item-variant/item-attributes.tsx`. Before accepting "pre-existing, not a defect," I checked `git log` on that file myself: last touched 2026-09-17, two commits before this one, `git status` shows it's not part of this diff at all. Confirmed, not assumed.
4. **Pass criterion 4.** Grepped for a second `MAX_PURCHASE_QUANTITY` anywhere new (found only the original, in a comment reference) and confirmed via `git status`/`git diff` that `product-detail/index.tsx` has zero changes.
5. **The `audit:tokens` N/A claim.** Read `scripts/auditTokenUsage.mjs` myself: `SCAN_ROOTS = [components, theme/components]` — literally cannot see `pages/` or `utils/`. Also ran it: 7 pre-existing hits, same baseline, none in the new files.

## What I could not verify

- I did not re-walk all 9 precedent citations the Tester checked line-by-line (e.g. every generated-field claim about `ShopperBasketsTypes.ProductItem`) — I spot-checked the two highest-stakes ones above instead of re-running a completed, unchanged review. That's a judgement call to avoid redoing work that hadn't changed, not a gap I'm hiding.
- No visual verification exists or is owed — confirmed structurally N/A above, not left unchecked.
- My two mutation checks were targeted single-branch edits mirroring the two most material claims, not an exhaustive mutation sweep — that sweep was the Tester's job and is already done (5 mutations, 3 clean, 2 found-then-fixed).

## Defects

None.

## Biggest residual risk in shipping this step

The backend half of this feature doesn't exist yet, and that's easy to lose track of once this merges. `TSD-SFCC-268` (the thing that actually populates `c_maxOrderQuantity`) is still `v0.1 Draft`, sign-off `Pending`, and a live sandbox probe found the field on zero real products — the hook isn't deployed anywhere. So the code you're merging is fully correct and fully tested against the *fallback* path, but the *real* path — reading an actual per-site BM value — has never run against real data and can't until another team ships the hook. It fails safe (anything not a clean positive finite number silently becomes 3, never a crash), which is the right call — but it also means if the real hook ships with a shape nobody guessed right here (say, BM stores it as the string `"3"` instead of a number), this function will quietly keep falling back to 3 forever, with nothing anywhere to flag that the "real" value is being ignored. Worth a one-line comment in the PR or a Jira note so SFCC-250 going "Done" doesn't imply enforcement changed for a real shopper today — it hasn't, and can't, until SFCC-268 ships.

## What Marcel is missing

Not from this step's own axes, but visible from here: `findings.md` line 107 (the pre-build gate) and the older shorthand HANDOFF.md struck out both described this exact function differently — a bare `??` fallback with **no** guard against `0`/negative, and "behind a shared helper" (i.e. promoted, not independent). What actually got built correctly follows the newer, more specific, authoritative plan.md §4 text instead (finite+positive guard, deliberately independent constant) — I traced this myself across all three documents and the resolution is sound. But it means `findings.md` — the artifact literally named "the gate" — now contains resolution language for this exact issue that the team's own more-recent, more-authoritative planning text overrode. Nobody needs to fix code over this, but if `findings.md` gets read again later as ground truth (rather than plan.md, which HANDOFF.md says wins), it will describe the wrong shape. A one-line strike-through in `findings.md` itself, pointing at HANDOFF.md's correction, would stop that from resurfacing as a false "regression" in some future audit.

- `/Users/marcel.a.n.navarro/Dev/zimmerMANN-skills/.runs/SFCC-11/findings.md` (lines 14-15, 38, 107)
